services.governmentEntity: Ministry of Health and Prevention (MoHAP) or the relevant emirate health authority; government hospitals issue certificates for births in government hospitals
services.jurisdiction: UAE-wide; emirate-specific health authority procedures apply
services.applicantType: UAE citizens and residents; also applicable where a UAE citizen/resident has a birth abroad
services.eligibility: Birth must be registered; residents generally have 30 days from birth to register
services.requiredDocuments: Parents’ Emirates IDs/passports, marriage certificate, hospital-issued stamped and signed birth notification; additional documents may be required by the health authority
services.instructions: 1. Obtain the hospital birth notification. 2. Government-hospital births: hospital issues the certificate. 3. Private-hospital births: apply to MoHAP or the relevant emirate health authority. 4. Overseas births: obtain the local certificate, translate/attest as needed and approach the UAE embassy.
services.officialFee: Fees depend on the issuing authority and service channel; confirm before applying.
services.officialTiming: Residents should register within 30 days of birth.
services.guidanceNote: Use the official portal’s ‘Having a baby’ page; ask the user where the birth occurred, whether the hospital was government or private, and the parents’ nationality/residency status.

services.serviceName: New Emirates ID card / addition to family record
services.governmentEntity: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP)
services.jurisdiction: UAE-wide
services.applicantType: UAE citizens and residents; newborn children of citizens and residents
services.eligibility: Newborn must be registered and added to the family record; apply through ICP
services.requiredDocuments: Child’s birth certificate, parents’ Emirates IDs, passport/visa details, marriage certificate where requested, passport photo if required
services.instructions: 1. Obtain the birth certificate. 2. Apply through ICP to add the child to the family record. 3. Complete biometrics/photo requirements if applicable. 4. Receive the Emirates ID.
services.officialFee: Emirates ID card fees are set by ICP; confirm the current fee during application.
services.officialTiming: Complete promptly after birth; residents should complete the full document set within 120 days.
services.guidanceNote: Ask whether the child is a UAE national or resident; direct UAE nationals to the online passport/Emirates ID route and residents to the family-sponsorship route.

sourceMetadata.dateCheckedColumnValue: Not published on the cited official page; confirm on the service page or with the responsible entity.

services.governmentEntity: ICP for UAE nationals/residents; UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs/embassy for births abroad; relevant health authority for birth certificate
services.jurisdiction: UAE-wide; overseas births handled through UAE embassies
services.applicantType: UAE citizens and residents and their newborn children
services.eligibility: Residence visa requires sponsorship by an eligible parent; medical fitness/security checks apply to applicants aged 18 and above, so not normally applicable to newborns
services.requiredDocuments: Birth certificate, parent’s passport/Emirates ID and residence visa, tenancy/proof of address where requested, marriage certificate, passport photos, health-insurance details
services.instructions: 1. Obtain the birth certificate. 2. Obtain the child’s passport. 3. Sponsor the child under the parent’s residence visa. 4. Apply for the residence visa and Emirates ID. 5. Arrange health insurance.
services.officialFee: Visa, Emirates ID and passport fees apply; confirm current amounts with ICP or the relevant authority.
services.officialTiming: Residents should complete birth certificate, passport, Emirates ID and visa within 120 days of birth.
services.guidanceNote: Identify the sponsoring parent, nationality, emirate and whether the family has insurance; sequence the steps as birth certificate, passport, visa, Emirates ID.

services.governmentEntity: Ministry of Health and Prevention; emirate health authorities and licensed healthcare providers
services.jurisdiction: UAE-wide; emirate-level providers and schedules may differ
services.applicantType: All children in the UAE; access and coverage depend on nationality, residency and insurance
services.eligibility: No general citizenship restriction for receiving vaccination through public or private providers; insurance or public-eligibility rules may apply
services.requiredDocuments: Birth certificate, Emirates ID/health card where available, insurance card, vaccination record, parent’s ID
services.instructions: 1. Register with a healthcare provider. 2. Attend scheduled well-baby and vaccination visits. 3. Keep the vaccination card updated. 4. Seek developmental checks and referrals where needed.
services.officialFee: Vaccines may be provided free through public services for eligible groups; private-provider fees and insurance coverage vary.
services.officialTiming: Follow the vaccination schedule and attend postnatal/child-health appointments as scheduled.
services.guidanceNote: Ask for emirate, public vs private provider, insurance status and vaccination history; explain that schedules and booking channels differ by emirate.

sourceMetadata.dateCheckedColumnValue: Not published on the cited official page; confirm on the service page or with the responsible entity.

services.serviceName: Student registration and admission to government schools
services.governmentEntity: Ministry of Education (MOE); emirate education authorities where applicable
services.jurisdiction: UAE-wide; admission rules and capacity can vary by emirate
services.applicantType: UAE nationals, UAE-passport holders, GCC citizens and certain decree-nationality children receive free education; expatriates may be admitted to grades 2–12 subject to conditions
services.eligibility: Expatriate admission to government schools requires a parent employed by a government, semi-government or local entity, at least 85% in Arabic, English and mathematics, valid residence visas, and available capacity; capacity is capped at 20%
services.requiredDocuments: Child’s Emirates ID, passport and residence visa, birth certificate, previous school reports/transcripts, vaccination record, parent’s Emirates ID, proof of address where requested
services.instructions: 1. Check age and grade eligibility. 2. Prepare documents. 3. Apply through MOE registration/admission during the announced period. 4. Await placement and complete enrolment.
services.officialFee: Free for eligible UAE nationals; non-UAE nationals attending government schools are fee-paying; the cited official page states AED 6,000.
services.officialTiming: Apply during the official registration/admission period; confirm current dates with MOE.
services.guidanceNote: Ask for the child’s date of birth, current grade, nationality/residency, emirate and prior school; check expatriate eligibility before recommending a government school.

services.serviceName: School age and grade placement rules
services.governmentEntity: Ministry of Education (MOE)
services.jurisdiction: UAE-wide
services.applicantType: All families applying for school admission
services.eligibility: KG1: at least age 4 by 31 August; KG2: age 5; Grade 1: age 6–8 by 31 August of the admission year
services.requiredDocuments: Birth certificate or passport proving date of birth, previous school records, transfer certificate, vaccination record
services.instructions: 1. Confirm the child’s age on 31 August. 2. Match prior schooling to the requested grade. 3. Obtain a transfer certificate if moving schools. 4. Submit documents with the admission application.
services.officialFee: Not applicable; this is an eligibility rule rather than a standalone paid service.
services.officialTiming: Age is assessed against 31 August of the admission year.
services.guidanceNote: Calculate eligible grade from date of birth; flag under-age applicants and transfer-certificate needs.

services.governmentEntity: Private schools; emirate education/regulatory authorities
services.jurisdiction: UAE-wide; fees, curricula and admission rules are school-specific
services.applicantType: UAE citizens, residents and other eligible students, subject to school admission criteria
services.eligibility: Each school sets admission, assessment and capacity requirements; confirm directly with the school
services.requiredDocuments: Child’s passport, Emirates ID, birth certificate, previous report cards, transfer certificate, vaccination record, parent’s ID/visa, proof of address
services.instructions: 1. Identify schools and curriculum. 2. Check availability, fees and admission requirements. 3. Submit the application. 4. Complete assessment/interview if required. 5. Accept the offer and pay registration fees.
services.officialFee: School-specific; confirm tuition, registration, transport and activity fees directly with the school.
services.officialTiming: Application and assessment dates are school-specific.
services.guidanceNote: Ask for emirate, curriculum, grade, budget and support needs; advise families to compare total annual cost, not tuition alone.

services.serviceName: Inclusive education and support for People of Determination
services.governmentEntity: Ministry of Education, schools, emirate education authorities and social-service entities
services.jurisdiction: UAE-wide; implementation and services can vary by emirate and school
services.applicantType: Students of determination; UAE citizens, residents and other eligible students as determined by the school/authority
services.eligibility: Equal educational opportunity is guaranteed; support depends on assessed needs and available school services
services.requiredDocuments: Emirates ID, birth certificate, previous school records, medical/psychological assessments, IEP if available, vaccination record
services.instructions: 1. Identify support needs. 2. Obtain assessments. 3. Contact the school or education authority. 4. Submit documents. 5. Attend assessment/planning meetings and agree an individual support plan.
services.officialFee: Support services in government schools are free; private-school support costs may vary.
services.officialTiming: Assessment and placement timelines depend on the school/authority.
services.guidanceNote: Ask whether the child has a diagnosis, assessment or IEP; explain inclusive education, resource rooms, specialist staff and assistive technology.

services.governmentEntity: Sharia courts, authorised marriage officials, Ministry of Justice and emirate judicial authorities
services.jurisdiction: UAE-wide; court/official procedures vary by emirate
services.applicantType: Muslim couples; eligibility depends on religion, nationality, guardianship and prior marital status
services.eligibility: Bride and groom must meet legal eligibility requirements; bride’s guardian and witnesses are required; premarital medical certificate is required
services.requiredDocuments: Emirates IDs, passports, birth certificates where requested, proof of marital status/divorce/death certificate if previously married, guardian’s ID, witnesses’ IDs, premarital medical certificate
services.instructions: 1. Complete premarital screening. 2. Prepare documents. 3. Book through a Sharia court, authorised official or online service. 4. Attend with guardian and witnesses. 5. Sign the contract, pay fees and obtain the certificate.
services.officialFee: Court/official fees apply; confirm the current schedule with the relevant court.
services.officialTiming: Book and complete before the intended marriage date; medical certificate must be valid.
services.guidanceNote: Ask for emirate, religion, prior marital status and whether the couple will use a court or authorised official; explain guardian and witness requirements.

services.governmentEntity: Relevant civil courts, personal-status authorities and authorised celebrants
services.jurisdiction: UAE-wide; Abu Dhabi, Dubai and other emirates may have different channels
services.applicantType: Non-Muslim couples and couples eligible under the applicable civil/personal-status rules
services.eligibility: Eligibility depends on nationality, religion, residency status and the applicable personal-status law
services.requiredDocuments: Passports, Emirates IDs/residence visas, proof of marital status, divorce/death certificates where applicable, affidavits/translations where required
services.instructions: 1. Identify the applicable route. 2. Check eligibility. 3. Apply through the relevant authority. 4. Attend and sign the contract. 5. Obtain the marriage certificate.
services.officialFee: Fees vary by authority and service; confirm before booking.
services.officialTiming: Appointment and certificate timelines vary by authority.
services.guidanceNote: Ask whether either party is Muslim, both are non-Muslim, their nationalities and emirate; route to civil or religious process accordingly.

services.governmentEntity: Emirates Health Services; Dubai Health; relevant health authorities
services.jurisdiction: UAE-wide; booking channels vary by emirate
services.applicantType: Couples intending an Islamic/Sharia marriage; other couples may use screening voluntarily
services.eligibility: Valid premarital medical certificate required before Sharia marriage registration; screening covers HIV, hepatitis, syphilis, thalassaemia and sickle-cell anaemia
services.requiredDocuments: Emirates ID, passport, and prior medical records if requested
services.instructions: 1. Book an appointment. 2. Attend screening. 3. Receive the medical certificate. 4. Submit it with the marriage application.
services.officialFee: Screening may be free or fee-based depending on eligibility and provider; confirm when booking.
services.officialTiming: Certificate must be valid at the time of marriage registration.
services.guidanceNote: Ask for emirate and marriage route; explain that the certificate is a prerequisite for Sharia marriage registration.

services.serviceName: Marriage certificate issuance / UAE marriage grant
services.governmentEntity: Ministry of Justice (eMarriage); Abu Dhabi Civil Family Court; Dubai Courts; Ministry of Community Empowerment for grant-related support
services.jurisdiction: UAE-wide; certificate channels vary by emirate
services.applicantType: Couples who completed a valid UAE marriage; grant eligibility is separate and subject to programme rules
services.eligibility: Certificate requires a completed marriage contract; grant eligibility is subject to official social-support criteria
services.requiredDocuments: Marriage contract, Emirates IDs, passports, bank/account details for grant applications where applicable
services.instructions: 1. Complete the marriage contract. 2. Apply for the certificate through eMarriage, Abu Dhabi Civil Family Court or Dubai Courts. 3. If eligible, apply for the marriage grant.
services.officialFee: Certificate fees may apply; the official page states eligible recipients may receive an AED 70,000 marriage grant in one instalment.
services.officialTiming: Apply soon after marriage; grant processing times depend on the programme.
services.guidanceNote: Ask whether the certificate is needed for visa sponsorship, banking, housing or a grant; identify the issuing emirate.

services.governmentEntity: Dubai Land Department/Ejari in Dubai; Abu Dhabi Municipality/Tawtheeq in Abu Dhabi; relevant emirate authority elsewhere
services.jurisdiction: Emirate-specific; Dubai uses Ejari, Abu Dhabi uses Tawtheeq
services.applicantType: Tenants and landlords/property owners
services.eligibility: A valid lease contract and identification documents are required; registration is required before utility connection
services.requiredDocuments: Tenant’s Emirates ID, passport/visa, signed tenancy contract, security deposit, landlord/property documents
services.instructions: 1. Find a property and agree the lease. 2. Sign the contract. 3. Register it with the relevant emirate authority. 4. Use the registered contract for utilities and other services.
services.officialFee: Registration and administrative fees may apply; confirm with the emirate authority.
services.officialTiming: Register before applying for utility connections.
services.guidanceNote: Ask for emirate, rented vs owned, new lease or renewal; explain Ejari for Dubai and Tawtheeq for Abu Dhabi.

services.serviceName: Electricity, water and utility service activation
services.governmentEntity: Etihad WE and other emirate utility providers; Dubai Electricity and Water Authority (DEWA) in Dubai
services.jurisdiction: UAE-wide; provider and process vary by emirate
services.applicantType: Tenants, property owners and authorised account holders
services.eligibility: Registered tenancy/ownership evidence is required; previous occupant’s account closure may be needed
services.requiredDocuments: Emirates ID, tenancy contract or title deed, previous occupant’s account-closing letter where applicable, payment method
services.instructions: 1. Register/transfer the tenancy or ownership record. 2. Apply to activate electricity, water and related services. 3. Submit documents and pay charges. 4. Schedule activation/transfer.
services.officialFee: Connection, security deposit and consumption charges may apply; confirm with the provider.
services.officialTiming: Allow time for account transfer/activation; confirm the provider’s current timeline.
services.guidanceNote: Ask for emirate and provider; for Etihad WE, list ID, tenancy/ownership documents and prior-occupant closure letter.

services.governmentEntity: ICP; employers, banks, schools and service providers as applicable
services.jurisdiction: UAE-wide
services.applicantType: UAE citizens and residents; sponsors and dependants
services.eligibility: Sponsors must maintain valid residence visas for dependants; certified lease/ownership evidence may be relevant to visa procedures
services.requiredDocuments: Emirates ID, new tenancy contract/Ejari or title deed, utility bill where requested, passport/visa documents
services.instructions: 1. Update address with ICP within one month. 2. Update banks, employer, school and insurers. 3. Verify dependants’ visa status. 4. Cancel or transfer visas formally when required.
services.officialFee: Address update may be free; visa-related fees may apply.
services.officialTiming: Notify ICP of address changes within one month.
services.guidanceNote: Ask whether the move is within or between emirates, whether the person owns or rents, and whether dependants’ visas need updating.

services.serviceName: Senior Emiratis services / home care and social support
services.governmentEntity: Ministry of Community Empowerment; emirate authorities; Red Crescent; health providers; Community Development Authority in Dubai
services.jurisdiction: UAE-wide; service availability and eligibility vary by emirate
services.applicantType: Primarily UAE nationals aged over 60; some services may be available to residents through health providers or private care
services.eligibility: Federal Law No. 9 of 2019 defines Senior Emiratis as UAE nationals over 60; entitlements include social care, medical care, preventive services, insurance, mobile nursing and assistive devices
services.requiredDocuments: Senior’s Emirates ID, passport/visa, medical reports, proof of income/social status where applicable, caregiver/family details
services.instructions: 1. Assess care needs. 2. Identify the relevant emirate service. 3. Apply for home care, rehabilitation, mobile-unit registration or social assistance. 4. Arrange follow-up and equipment.
services.officialFee: Some public services are free for eligible seniors; private care and some transport services may charge fees.
services.officialTiming: Application and assessment timelines depend on the service and emirate.
services.guidanceNote: Ask whether the parent is a UAE national or resident, age, mobility, medical needs and emirate; distinguish public entitlements from private care.

services.serviceName: Home healthcare, rehabilitation and elderly health services
services.governmentEntity: Ministry of Health and Prevention; emirate health authorities; Sheikh Khalifa Medical City; Tawam Hospital; Dubai Health; Red Crescent
services.jurisdiction: UAE-wide; provider eligibility differs by emirate
services.applicantType: UAE nationals for certain public home-care services; expatriate residents may access services through Dubai Health or private providers
services.eligibility: Clinical need and provider eligibility determine home care, rehabilitation and specialist referrals
services.requiredDocuments: Emirates ID, insurance card, medical reports, prescriptions, hospital discharge summary, caregiver contact details
services.instructions: 1. Obtain a medical assessment. 2. Request rehabilitation, nursing, physiotherapy or home care. 3. Apply through the relevant provider. 4. Coordinate medication, appointments and equipment.
services.officialFee: Public eligibility and insurance coverage vary; private services may charge fees.
services.officialTiming: Referral and scheduling times depend on clinical urgency and provider capacity.
services.guidanceNote: Ask whether care is short-term post-hospital or long-term; identify emirate, insurance and whether the parent is a national or resident.

services.governmentEntity: Ministry of Community Empowerment; Abu Dhabi Social Support Programme where applicable
services.jurisdiction: UAE-wide; Abu Dhabi has a specific social-support application route
services.applicantType: Primarily eligible UAE nationals; eligibility and benefits depend on income, family and social circumstances
services.eligibility: UAE nationals can apply under the social welfare policy; eligibility assessment considers income, family and social circumstances
services.requiredDocuments: Emirates ID, family book/proof of nationality where applicable, income/financial details, medical/disability reports, housing details, bank account details
services.instructions: 1. Check eligibility. 2. Register through UAE Pass where required. 3. Apply through the Ministry of Community Empowerment or relevant emirate programme. 4. Submit documents and await assessment.
services.officialFee: No general fee is stated on the cited official page; confirm during application.
services.officialTiming: Processing times depend on the programme and assessment.
services.guidanceNote: Ask for nationality, income, dependants, housing and medical needs; explain that social welfare is primarily for eligible UAE nationals.

services.governmentEntity: General Pension and Social Security Authority (GPSSA); employers; relevant pension authorities
services.jurisdiction: UAE-wide; rules differ between public and private sectors and by nationality
services.applicantType: UAE and GCC nationals in covered employment; private-sector expatriates generally receive end-of-service benefits rather than GPSSA pension
services.eligibility: Federal pension is for eligible Emiratis and other GCC nationals; standard retirement is generally age 60 with 15 years of insured service; early retirement rules differ by gender
services.requiredDocuments: Emirates ID, passport, labour card/employment contract, bank details, employer clearance/NOC, service records
services.instructions: 1. Confirm coverage and eligibility. 2. Submit retirement/pension application through employer and/or GPSSA. 3. Complete clearance. 4. Receive pension or end-of-service payment.
services.officialFee: Contribution and benefit rules apply; end-of-service gratuity is calculated under applicable rules.
services.officialTiming: Apply before or upon end of service; processing depends on employer and authority.
services.guidanceNote: Ask whether the person is a UAE/GCC national or expatriate, public or private sector, years of service and retirement reason.

services.governmentEntity: General Pension and Social Security Authority (GPSSA)
services.jurisdiction: UAE-wide
services.applicantType: UAE nationals and eligible GCC nationals working in the UAE
services.eligibility: Employers must register Emirati employees from the first month of employment; standard retirement age 60 with 15 years of insured service; men may retire early at 55 with 20 years; women at 50 with 20 years
services.requiredDocuments: Emirates ID, passport, employment records, bank details, employer clearance documents
services.instructions: 1. Confirm GPSSA registration. 2. Check age/service eligibility. 3. Submit retirement request through employer/GPSSA. 4. Complete clearance and receive benefits.
services.officialFee: Pension contributions and benefit calculations apply under GPSSA rules.
services.officialTiming: Retirement applications should be submitted through the employer/GPSSA before or at end of service.
services.guidanceNote: Ask for nationality, sector, age, insured service and whether retirement is voluntary or employer-initiated.

services.governmentEntity: ICP and relevant emirate authorities
services.jurisdiction: UAE-wide; specific emirate retirement programmes may have additional criteria
services.applicantType: Retired expatriates and eligible applicants; dependants may be sponsored subject to rules
services.eligibility: Applicant must meet the financial/property/investment criteria of the applicable retirement visa route; medical fitness and security checks apply to applicants aged 18 and above
services.requiredDocuments: Passport, current visa, Emirates ID, proof of income/investment/property as applicable, health insurance, tenancy or ownership documents
services.instructions: 1. Check eligibility. 2. Prepare financial/property evidence. 3. Apply through ICP or relevant authority. 4. Complete medical testing and Emirates ID issuance. 5. Receive visa stamping.
services.officialFee: Government fees apply; confirm the current visa and Emirates ID fees.
services.officialTiming: Processing time depends on application completeness and authority workload.
services.guidanceNote: Ask whether the applicant is already resident, their age, income/assets and dependants; explain medical and security requirements.

services.serviceName: Death registration and death certificate issuance
services.governmentEntity: Police; government morgue; Emirates Health Services or relevant emirate health authority; UAE embassies for deaths abroad
services.jurisdiction: UAE-wide; emirate health authority procedures apply; overseas deaths handled through embassies
services.applicantType: Family members, legal representatives or authorised persons reporting a death
services.eligibility: Out-of-hospital deaths must be reported to police immediately; official death certificate requires morgue and police documentation
services.requiredDocuments: Deceased’s Emirates ID/passport, hospital or police documents, morgue declaration, police NOC, family member’s ID
services.instructions: 1. If outside hospital, call 999 immediately. 2. Police report and transfer to morgue. 3. Obtain morgue declaration and police NOC. 4. Apply for the official death certificate. 5. For overseas deaths, obtain local certificate and contact the UAE embassy.
services.officialFee: Certificate issuance fees may apply; confirm with the issuing authority.
services.officialTiming: Report out-of-hospital deaths immediately by calling 999; apply for the certificate promptly.
services.guidanceNote: Ask whether the death occurred in hospital, at home or abroad; explain the 999 step and the police/morgue/health-authority sequence.

services.governmentEntity: Police; Public Prosecution where applicable; municipality/cemetery authorities
services.jurisdiction: UAE-wide; cemetery and religious procedures vary by emirate
services.applicantType: Family members or authorised representatives of the deceased
services.eligibility: Natural deaths require a burial permit from district police; unnatural deaths require forensic report, police NOC and Public Prosecution letter
services.requiredDocuments: Death certificate/morgue declaration, police NOC, forensic/prosecution documents where applicable, deceased’s Emirates ID/passport, family member’s ID
services.instructions: 1. Obtain death documentation. 2. Obtain the burial permit. 3. Arrange burial through the relevant cemetery/municipality. 4. Follow religious and family arrangements.
services.officialFee: Burial/cemetery charges may apply; confirm with the cemetery or municipality.
services.officialTiming: Obtain permits before burial; timing depends on police/forensic procedures.
services.guidanceNote: Ask whether the death was natural or unexpected, the emirate, religion and preferred cemetery; explain permit requirements.

services.governmentEntity: UAE courts/notaries; banks; Dubai Land Department; RTA/traffic authorities; insurers; relevant emirate authorities
services.jurisdiction: UAE-wide; inheritance rules can differ by religion, nationality, will and asset type
services.applicantType: Heirs, executors, legal representatives and beneficiaries
services.eligibility: Legal succession procedures and asset-specific transfer requirements apply; a will may affect distribution
services.requiredDocuments: Death certificate, deceased’s Emirates ID/passport, heirs’ IDs/passports, marriage certificate, heirs’ birth certificates, will/succession documents, asset/ownership documents
services.instructions: 1. Obtain the death certificate. 2. Identify assets and liabilities. 3. Obtain legal succession/inheritance documents. 4. Transfer or update bank, property, vehicle, insurance and utility records.
services.officialFee: Court, notary, translation, attestation and asset-transfer fees may apply.
services.officialTiming: No single official deadline; act promptly to prevent account restrictions and asset-transfer delays.
services.guidanceNote: Ask whether there is a will, which emirate applies, whether assets are in the UAE or abroad, and the deceased’s religion/nationality; explain that procedures vary.

services.governmentEntity: ICP; deceased’s embassy or consulate for expatriates
services.jurisdiction: UAE-wide
services.applicantType: Sponsors, family members and legal representatives of deceased residents
services.eligibility: Sponsors must formally cancel visas; a widow and children on the deceased husband’s visa may be eligible for a one-year extension
services.requiredDocuments: Death certificate, deceased’s Emirates ID/passport, sponsor/dependent visa details, family member’s Emirates ID, embassy documents where applicable
services.instructions: 1. Obtain the death certificate. 2. Notify the embassy/consulate for an expatriate. 3. Cancel the deceased’s residence visa and Emirates ID. 4. Arrange transfer or cancellation of dependants’ visas. 5. Update banks and service providers.
services.officialFee: Visa cancellation may be free or subject to administrative fees; confirm with ICP.
services.officialTiming: Arrange cancellation promptly; dependants’ status should be addressed before visa expiry.
services.guidanceNote: Ask whether the deceased was a national or resident, whether they sponsored dependants, and whether the family intends to remain in the UAE.
